title: Best Hill Stations in India: Where to Go and When
seoTitle: Best Hill Stations in India: Where to Go and When | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: The best hill stations in India by region and season: Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Darjeeling, Gangtok, Munnar, Ooty, Coorg and more, with when to go.
description: A guide to the best hill stations in India, grouped by region: the Himalayan towns of Himachal, Uttarakhand and Kashmir, the hills of Darjeeling, Sikkim and the Northeast, the Nilgiris and Western Ghats of the south, and Mahabaleshwar, Mount Abu and Pachmarhi in the west and centre, with the best season for each and how to choose.
dek: India's hill stations range from colonial summer capitals to tea towns and Himalayan villages. Here is how to pick the right one for your month and your kind of holiday.

hero.alt: Shimla spread along its ridge, Himachal Pradesh

intro: A hill station, in the Indian sense, is a town built up in the hills as a cool-weather retreat, many of them developed in the 19th century. Today the name covers everything from busy resort towns such as Shimla and Ooty to quieter places like Kausani or Yercaud.

The best choice depends on the month, how far you want to travel and what you enjoy: snow, tea gardens, walks, lakes or simply cool air. This guide groups the leading hill stations by region and links to our full destination guides.
quickAnswer: The best hill stations in India include Shimla, Manali and Dharamshala in Himachal Pradesh; Mussoorie and Nainital in Uttarakhand; Gulmarg and Pahalgam in Kashmir; Darjeeling and Gangtok in the eastern Himalaya; Shillong in Meghalaya; Ooty and Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu; Munnar in Kerala; Coorg in Karnataka; and Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. Himalayan towns suit March to June and October to December; the southern hills are pleasant most of the year.
takeaways: Himalayan hill stations are best from March to June and October to December; many see snow in mid-winter.
The Nilgiris, Munnar and Coorg are pleasant for most of the year, but very wet in the monsoon.
Western Ghats hills near Mumbai and Pune are at their greenest in the monsoon.
Busy towns like Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie and Ooty get crowded in May, June and long weekends; book ahead.
Quieter alternatives exist near almost every famous hill station.

sections.heading: The Himalayan hill stations
paras: Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand have the densest choice of hill stations, most within a day's travel of Delhi. Shimla and Mussoorie are the classic colonial towns; Manali is the gateway to high passes and snow; Nainital and the Kumaon towns such as Kausani and Ranikhet offer views of Nanda Devi and the high Himalaya. Kashmir's Gulmarg and Pahalgam are more alpine, with meadows and forests.

sections.heading: Western and central India
list: Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani: viewpoints and strawberry farms, about five to six hours from Mumbai.
Lonavala and Matheran: short trips from Mumbai and Pune; Matheran bans private vehicles.
Mount Abu: Rajasthan's only hill station, with Nakki Lake and the Dilwara temples.
Saputara: Gujarat's hill station in the Sahyadri.
Pachmarhi: Madhya Pradesh's hill station in the Satpura range.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to June: the classic summer season across the Himalaya and the south; busiest in May and June.
July to September: heavy rain in the Western Ghats and Meghalaya, and landslide risk in the Himalaya; best for monsoon trips near Mumbai and Pune.
October to December: clear skies and long views in the Himalaya; the post-monsoon south is lush.
December to February: snow is likely in higher Himalayan resorts, though never guaranteed; the southern hills are cool and dry.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates before you drive, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeway timings and pass openings change; check the official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; evenings in the hills are cool.
Book stays ahead for May, June, Christmas and New Year, when popular towns fill up.
packing: Warm layers and a light jacket

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in India?
faqs.a: It depends on the season and what you want; Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Darjeeling, Gangtok, Munnar, Ooty and Coorg are among the most popular.

faqs.q: Which hill station is best in summer?
faqs.a: Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling, Gangtok and Ooty are popular summer escapes; Gulmarg and Pahalgam are green from April to June.

faqs.q: Which hill stations have snow in winter?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Manali, Auli, Kufri and Narkanda near Shimla, and Tawang often see snow between December and February, though snowfall varies each year.

faqs.q: Which hill stations are good for a short trip?
faqs.a: Mussoorie and Nainital from Delhi, Lonavala and Matheran from Mumbai, Nandi Hills and Coorg from Bengaluru, and Yelagiri from Chennai.

faqs.q: Are hill stations crowded in May and June?
faqs.a: Yes, the famous ones are; go midweek, book early, or choose quieter towns nearby.
